sections.title: No ePassport? Finish in a branch
Take a photo of your face
Why we ask, and how it's protected

beats.vo: In this video we will show you how to open an account and verify your identity online.

moments.sub: And verify your identity, step by step.
moments.why: the app's own three-part journey screen tells viewers where this ends up

beats.vo: Before you begin make sure you have the correct documentation: An Australian phone number An Australian address A valid Australian Visa This would be all Australian visa’s except a visitor visa. An ePassport

moments.why: four parallel essentials of equal weight; the checklist a sound-off viewer can pause on

moments.super: Any visa except a visitor visa.
moments.sub: Plus an ePassport.
moments.why: the visa rule is the one exception to flag, and the app shows the same list

beats.vo: To check if you have an ePassport look for a small rectangle with a circle and line on the front and back cover of the passport. This is a chip that stores your photo and identity details.

moments.sub: On the front or back cover of your passport.
moments.why: the chip mark drawn full size is the one thing viewers must recognise on their own passport

moments.sub: It stores your photo and identity details.
moments.why: the app's illustrated passport shows the same mark in context

beats.vo: If you don’t have an ePassport, you can still start the application online with a standard passport and then visit a branch to complete your identity verification

moments.super: No ePassport? Finish in a branch.
moments.sub: Start with a standard passport, then verify in a branch.
moments.why: two steps in order, online then branch; nothing is struck because both are valid

beats.vo: You will be asked to select one of the options below regarding your status in Australia: You have lived in Australia for over a year. You arrived in Australia less than 1 year ago. You are moving to Australia soon – planning to arrive in the next 14 days

moments.sub: Pick one of three options.
moments.why: the real options screen, so viewers recognise it on their phone

moments.sub: Choose 'Living in Australia'.
moments.why: phone text is unreadable at this scale; restate the option in large type with the app's label

moments.super: Arrived less than a year ago.
moments.sub: Choose 'Recently arrived'.
moments.why: second option, same pattern so it reads as a set

moments.sub: Choose 'Moving to Australia soon'.
moments.why: third option, same pattern

beats.vo: You will then need to scan a photo of your passport. Ensure you’re in good lighting to avoid glare or reflections. Hold the photo page of your passport up to the scanning area indicated on the screen and select scan passport.

moments.super: Take a photo of your passport.
moments.why: the step screen as the viewer meets it

moments.sub: Use good light, away from reflections.
moments.why: the wrong way first, with the cross paired to words

moments.sub: Fit the photo page inside the frame.
moments.why: the right way, a clear capture, with the tick paired to words

beats.vo: Please provide your contact details: Mobile number Email address Australian address We’ll use these details to contact you and send your debit card once it’s ready.

moments.sub: Mobile number, email and Australian address.
moments.why: the form scrolls through the three fields as they are read

moments.sub: So use your Australian address.
moments.why: card to mail to home explains why the address matters

beats.vo: You will be asked to verify your identity. To complete this step, you will need to: Tap ‘Scan passport chip’ Wait until you see ‘Ready to scan’ Hold your passport against the back of your phone. If nothing happens, move your phone around slowly until it vibrates

moments.sub: You'll scan your passport chip.
moments.why: the numbered how-to screen opens the step

moments.sub: Then wait for 'Ready to scan'.
moments.why: the button names in large type, since the app text is too small to read

moments.super: Hold your passport to your phone.
moments.sub: Against the back of the phone.
moments.why: the Ready to scan sheet is the moment to place the passport

moments.sub: Move your phone around until it vibrates.
moments.why: the tip that rescues a stuck scan stands alone so scrubbers find it

beats.vo: if you are a USA or Malaysian passport holder you will need to open your passport before scanning. Hold still until the scan finishes. This may take 5-10 seconds

moments.sub: Open it before you scan.
moments.why: a condition that applies only to some viewers, so it gets its own plain card
the 60% hold-still sheet as the viewer will see it

moments.sub: Your phone vibrates when it's done.
moments.why: the buzz and the verified screen close the scan, with the tick paired to words

beats.vo: Then you will need to take a photo of your face, using the camera on your device. Please ensure you have removed glasses, hats or any items that might be covering your face.

moments.super: Take a photo of your face.
moments.sub: Use the camera on your phone.
moments.why: the app's selfie instructions screen

moments.asset: Selfie with a hat on, crossed out, CBA to supply
moments.super: Hat or glasses on: not accepted.
moments.sub: Remove anything covering your face.
moments.why: the don't of the pair; no hat-on screen exists yet
the real capture as the do, with the tick paired to words

beats.vo: You will now need to provide your employment details and information regarding your tax residency.

moments.why: first of two short question sets

moments.cue: and information regarding your tax residency
moments.super: Tell us where you pay tax.
moments.why: second question set, one plain super each

beats.vo: Australian banks are required by law to collect this information. This information is collected in line with our privacy obligations, to find out more search ‘Group Privacy Statement’ on the CommBank website to see how we protect your information.

moments.sub: All Australian banks must collect this.
moments.why: one reassuring headline: it is the law, not CommBank being nosy

moments.sub: In line with our privacy obligations.
moments.why: protection gets its own card so the reassurance lands

moments.sub: On the CommBank website.
moments.why: the exact search term on screen, held long enough to copy down

beats.vo: You will then need to create a password and PIN so you can securely access your account and the CommBank app.

moments.why: the password screen as the viewer meets it

moments.sub: To access your account and the CommBank app.
moments.why: the PIN screen on the opposite side reads as the next step

beats.vo: Once approved, your account will be ready to use, and your debit card will be sent to your nominated Australian address. Welcome to Australia and welcome to CommBank.

moments.why: success screen with the tick paired to words

moments.super: Your debit card is on its way.
moments.sub: To your Australian address.
moments.why: pays off the address step from earlier

moments.sub: And welcome to CommBank.
moments.why: the warm close; the Beacon lockup is placed by hand on this card
